## What have you built?

Thank you for trying DDESONN. If you have built or trained a model, nice work.
Please tell me what you have built or achieved with the package. I would be very
grateful to hear about useful applications, interesting results and ideas for
what we could build next. Results that did not work out can be useful too.

Following these recent updates, I strongly encourage contributions: reproducible
experiments, bug reports, fixes, documentation, visualizations and suggestions.
There are many directions I would like to explore with this framework, and I
welcome conversations about good ideas, practical needs and opportunities to
collaborate. A small example or a clear issue is a useful place to start.

## Reach out or connect

- [Connect with me on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mathewfok).
  Please include a short note mentioning DDESONN when you add me.
- [Email me](mailto:quiksilver67213@yahoo.com).
- [Share an application, suggestion or reproducible issue on GitHub](https://github.com/MatHatter/DDESONN/issues).
- [Contribute a pull request](https://github.com/MatHatter/DDESONN/pulls).

Tell me what you tried, what you learned and what you would like the package to
do. For a bug or performance claim, include the version, settings, data/split
provenance and a small reproducible example when you can.

## Ideas I still want to explore

The neural-network visualization idea remains on my list: a view of the model's
structure with equations and relevant settings integrated into the network. This remains a
planned idea; the package does not yet provide that proposed visualization tool.
Suggestions and contributions are welcome.

I also want to update my separate
[OLR — Optimal Linear Regression package](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=olr).
OLR is another project of mine; it is not part of DDESONN and is not required to
use this workbench.

## If you find a useful SSM application

The optional state-space/sequence encoder remains experimental and off by
default. Our current benchmarks have not shown a meaningful improvement over the
baseline. If you find a useful SSM application or a reproducible benefit, please
let me know. Independent results showing no benefit are welcome as well.

For comparisons, use matched data splits and settings, keep related or repeated
inputs out of opposing partitions, repeat seeds where practical and report the
variation. A single successful run is not sufficient evidence of an advantage.
See the repository's
[SSM context](https://github.com/MatHatter/DDESONN#optional-native-r-sequence-encoder)
and current research limitations before interpreting performance claims.

## Keep your work before ending the app session

Recent runs is a separate in-memory archive for the latest 10 completed models
and CSV runs in your current browser session. Clearing the saved-model workspace
does not clear it. You can restore a recent item, remove one entry, or clear
recent history without changing active workspaces or files on disk.

This archive is not permanent storage. Restore a model and use **Save & export**
to download its `.rds` if you want to keep it after the Shiny session ends. Save
prediction CSVs separately when you need to compare them with outcomes later.
